sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Country/MB-Locality/MB-Region unique-values filter dropdown (📊): cells holding more than one flag (a multi-event Country cell, or a Region cell where a third-party userscript decorates both a subdivision AND its sovereign state with custom flag icons, e.g. "Noord-Holland, Kingdom of the Netherlands") now show all of their flags in the dropdown instead of none. countryFlagMap/areaIconMap (see WIP.1/WIP.2) previously keyed each flag by a label parsed from that single flag's own text, but the dropdown's unique value is always the whole cell's combined text — a multi-flag cell's combined value never matched any single flag's label, so no icon was shown at all. Both maps are now keyed by the cell's full getCleanColumnText() value (exactly how the dropdown's own value list is built) and bundle every flag found in that cell into one wrapper.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: MB-Locality/MB-Region (and Begin/End variants) unique-values filter dropdown (📊): entries now show the subdivision flag icon injected by third-party userscripts like "MusicBrainz: More Flags Everywhere", matching the icon already shown in the table cells. The dropdown's flag-decoration feature previously only recognized exact Country column names, so it never ran at all for Locality/Region columns; its cell scan was also hardcoded to elements, which would have missed the markup these third-party icons actually use even if it had run. Column-name matching is now suffix-based (matching this file's own _flagRegionColumnTrios convention for the same column family), which as a side effect also fixes the Country dropdown never decorating a 'Release country' column.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Country column unique-values filter dropdown (📊): the flag icon next to each country name now renders identically to the flag in the table cell. Previously only the span's CSS class was copied into the dropdown clone, which relies on MusicBrainz's own stylesheet cascading correctly wherever the clone lands — the dropdown panel sits outside #content/table.tbl and in a smaller font-size context, so the flag could come out looking flatter/blanker than the real one. Now the resolved visual (background sprite, size, border, vertical-align, …) is read directly from the live table-cell flag via getComputedStyle() — including a ::before/::after pseudo-element fallback — and baked as inline styles onto the dropdown clone, so it is pixel-identical regardless of where MusicBrainz's CSS rule is scoped.
